column15: Observed DST in 1916–1918, 1920, 1940–1948 (as part of Germany between 1940–1945) and since 1980.

column29: Observed DST in 1916–1918 when it was a part of {{flag|Austria-Hungary}}, in 1941–1945 and since 1983 when it was part of the {{flag|Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia}}.
column39: {{Main article|Daylight saving time in Canada}} Some regions in {{flag|Quebec}}, east of 63° west longitude, most of {{flag|Saskatchewan}}, and some areas in {{flag|British Columbia}} and {{flag|Nunavut}} (Southampton Island) do not observe DST. Saskatchewan, however, observes Central Time even though it is located in the Mountain Time Zone, meaning it effectively observes DST year round.
column44: Observed DST in 1927–1946 (excluding {{flag|Easter Island}} which observed it in 1932–1946) and from 1968–2015. Chile observed year-round DST in 2015, but reintroduced regular DST in 2016. Magallanes Region does not observe DST since December 2016.
column45: Observed DST in 1940–1941,1986–1991. In 1980, its UTC+5, UTC+6, UTC+7, and UTC+9 zones (the entire country) all changed to UTC+8.
column54: Observed DST in 1916–1918 when it was a part of {{flag|Austria-Hungary}}, in 1941–1945 and since 1983.
column57: Observed DST since 1975. {{flag|Northern Cyprus}} maintained permanent DST from September 2016 to October 2017.
column65: Observed DST in 1940–1945, 1957–2010 and 2014–2015. An attempt to restore daylight saving after Ramadan was rejected by the Egyptian parliament on July 4, 2016 and currently has no plans to use DST in the future.
column74: {{Main article|Daylight saving time in Fiji}} Observed DST in 1998–2000 and since 2009.
column86: Observed DST since 1980. Follows European Union practice as part of the Kingdom of Denmark, hence start & end times correspond to 01:00 UTC on the respective Sunday. See Daylight saving time in the Americas—GreenlandQaanaaq uses US and Canada rules. Danmarkshavn has not observed DST since 1995.
column100: Observed DST in 1916–1920, 1941–1950, 1954–1957 and since 1980. The government considered abolishing DST in 2017, moving Hungary to the UTC+02:00 (EET) year-round, but there are no official plans to do so yet. This would be problematic considering DST switch is coordinated on a EU level.
column102: Observed DST during World War 2, from 1942–1945.
column105: {{Main article|Daylight saving time in Iran}} Observed DST in 1977–1980, 1991–2005 and since 2008.
column108: {{Main article|Israel Summer Time}} Observed DST in 1940–1946, 1948–1957, 1974–1975 and since 1985.
column114: Observed DST in 1973–1979 and 1985–2011. In 2012 changed time zone to UTC+03:00, effectively going on permanent DST. Returned to UTC+02:00 on Dec 20, 2013, and has observed DST since 2014.
column133: Observed DST in 1933–1981. The time zone in Malaysia has changed and varied a lot in the past.
column138: Observed DST in 1980. Currently Does not observe DST.
column141: {{Main article|Daylight saving time in Mexico}} Has observed DST since 1996, but {{flag|Baja California}} has observed DST since 1976. {{flag|Sonora}} discontinued the observance in 1997 and {{flag|Quintana Roo}} in 2014. Durango, Coahuila, Nuevo León and Tamaulipas observed DST in 1988. Locations less than 20 km from the US border use U.S. DST. {{flag|Baja California}} also uses the U.S. DST.
column147: Observed DST 1941–1945 and since 1983 when it was part of the {{flag|Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia}}.
column149: Observed DST in 1939–1945, 1950, 1967, 1974, 1974–1976, and 2008–2018. DST was stopped during Ramadan.
column152: Observed DST in 1942–1943. Does not observe DST but implemented winter time in 1994 in all regions except Zambezi. DST was removed in 2017.
column165: Observed DST in 1941–1945 and since 1983 when it was part of the {{flag|Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia}}.
column166: Observed DST in 1916, 1940–1945, 1959–1965 and since 1980. Follows European Union practice, although not a member.
column168: Observed DST in 1942–1945 as a part of {{flag|British Raj}}. Also observed in 2002 and from 2008–2009.
column173: Observed DST since 1975. Current start and end dates last updated in 2013.
column182: Observed DST in 1917–1919, 1921 (some areas) and 1981–2010. In 2011–2014, used permanent DST. In 2014, left permanent DST and switched to permanent standard time.
column192: {{Main article|Daylight saving time in Samoa}} Observed DST since 2010.
column197: Observed DST in 1941–1945 and since 1983 (did not observe DST as part of Yugoslavia, from 1918–1941, and 1945–1983).
column200: Observed DST in 1933–1935 by adding 20 minutes to standard time. On January 1, 1936, country changed their time zone to UTC+07:20.
column204: Observed DST in 1916–1918 when it was a part of {{flag|Austria-Hungary}}, in 1941–1945 and since 1983.
column212: Observed DST in 1917–1919, 1924, 1926–1929, 1937–1946, 1949 and since 1974. On {{flag|Canary Islands}} DST observed since 1980.
column213: Observed DST during the Second World War, from 1942–1945 just as the rest of the Indian subcontinent.
